content: The true effect of an intervention may differ significantly from the estimated effect. When there is very low certainty in the evidence, confidence in the effect estimate is minimal, and the actual effect is likely to vary substantially from the predicted outcome. The World Health Organization (WHO) has issued recommendations for the prevention and treatment of postpartum hemorrhage, which were accessed in November 2018. Gallos et al. conducted a network meta-analysis in 2018 to evaluate the effectiveness of uterotonic agents in preventing postpartum hemorrhage. Similarly, Downe et al. performed a systematic qualitative review in 2018 to understand what matters most to women during childbirth. Another review by Finlayson et al. explored the perspectives of women and healthcare providers regarding interventions for postpartum hemorrhage prevention. Lawrie et al. conducted a systematic review in 2018 to assess the cost-effectiveness of uterotonic agents for preventing postpartum hemorrhage. Bradley et al. evaluated the cost-effectiveness of misoprostol in low-resource settings in 2007, while Lubinga et al. examined the potential cost-effectiveness of prenatal misoprostol distribution in Uganda in 2015. Lang et al. analyzed the cost consequences of misoprostol for postpartum hemorrhage prevention in low-resource settings in 2015. Sutherland et al. investigated the community-based distribution of misoprostol for postpartum hemorrhage prevention and treatment, focusing on cost-effectiveness, mortality, and morbidity reduction in 2010. Another study by Sutherland and Bishai in 2009 assessed the cost-effectiveness of misoprostol and prenatal iron supplementation as maternal mortality interventions in rural India. Vlassoff et al. evaluated the cost-effectiveness of two postpartum hemorrhage prevention interventions in Senegal in 2016. Gallos et al. also conducted a network meta-analysis and cost-effectiveness analysis of uterotonic drugs for postpartum hemorrhage prevention, with findings published in 2018. The British National Formulary (72nd edition) provided additional guidance on uterotonic use during this period. Voon et al. performed a cost-effectiveness analysis of carbetocin during cesarean sections in high-volume maternity units in 2018. The WHO has published recommendations on uterotonics for postpartum hemorrhage prevention, including assumptions for interventions in the One Health Tool (drafted in January 2016). The State of Inequality report, accessed in November 2018, highlights disparities in reproductive, maternal, newborn, and child health. The Prevention of Postpartum Hemorrhage Initiative (POPPHI) evaluated the safety and feasibility of using oxytocin in a Uniject™ device for active management of the third stage of labor in Mali. Lastly, the WHO's 20th Model List of Essential Medicines, updated in August 2017, includes key medications for postpartum hemorrhage prevention.
